neighbours.label: A list with a tilt: nouns for a young person or an animal (boy, girl, rabbit, snake, ox), strongest when the noun is the first part of a compound or derived word ('boyhood', 'girlhood', 'rabbit costume', 'snake-like', 'ox cart'). The same compound frames built on other nouns ('childhood', 'pirate costume', 'stone-like') stay quiet. The - pole is ' giant'.
fire: The old sailor often talked about his boyhood on the docks.
For the school play, Marta sewed a rabbit mask out of grey felt.
The dancer crossed the stage with a slow, snake-like sway.
Two brothers loaded the ox wagon with sacks of grain.
My aunt kept a diary all through her girlhood in Cork.
The toddler refused to take off his rabbit slippers at bedtime.
The actress played a boy soldier in her first film.
A carved snake handle curled around the lid of the jar.
quiet: The old sailor often talked about his childhood on the docks.
For the school play, Marta sewed a clown mask out of grey felt.
The dancer crossed the stage with a slow, dream-like sway.
Two brothers loaded the hay wagon with sacks of grain.
My aunt kept a diary all through her widowhood in Cork.
The toddler refused to take off his woolly slippers at bedtime.
The actress played a foot soldier in her first film.
A carved ivory handle curled around the lid of the jar.

notes: Card: ' ox' x4, ' rabbit' x4, ' boy' x4, ' Boy' x2, ' sex' x2, '-boy' x2; also 'woman' in 'womanizing', 'egg-smooth', 'puppy'. Probes: rabbit costume 0.94, boyhood 0.75, girlhood 0.70, snake-like 0.56, ox cart 0.39; as plain nouns: 'The rabbit ran' 0.45, 'The boy ran' 0.30; childhood 0.03, pirate costume 0.005, stone-like 0.14, puppy eyes 0.15. I did not find one distinction that covers boy/girl, animals, 'sex' and 'egg', so this is a list. The near misses test the frame without the nouns, not the nouns outside the frame.
